content: Studies indicate that ACE inhibitors and ARBs are frequently not prescribed at their maximum tolerated doses, which can reduce their effectiveness in slowing the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). For patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) above 73 m² and without significant albuminuria, these medications provide limited benefits. To achieve optimal therapeutic outcomes, it is crucial to maximize the dosage of these drugs within the limits of patient tolerance. If serum creatinine levels increase without the presence of hyperkalemia, it is generally recommended to continue treatment unless there are substantial adverse effects that necessitate discontinuation.
